message.content: Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora (cats) and Perissodactyla (odd‑toed ungulates), respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes all of those orders (Artiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Chiroptera, Cetartiodactyla, Carnivora, and others). This ancestor lived roughly 90–100 million years ago during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. In a broader sense, the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria) is even older, but the Laurasiatherian ancestor is the most specific common ancestor shared by lions and zebras.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor of lion and zebra. We need to answer. The question is about evolutionary biology. Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga). They belong to different families: lions are Felidae (cat family), zebras are Equidae (horse family). Both are mammals, order Carnivora vs order Perissodactyla. Actually zebra is an odd-toed ungulate (Perissodactyla). So their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Or maybe the last common ancestor of the two orders? The last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all Laurasiatheria? Actually Carnivora is part of Laurasiatheria, as is Perissodactyla. So the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. But we can say the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). But if we want more specific: the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both orders is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all Laurasiatheria. That might be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders that are part of Laurasiatheria: Artiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Chiroptera, Cetartiodactyla, Carnivora, etc. So the last common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria, which lived around 90 million years ago. But we can also mention that the last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older (~100-120 million years). But the question likely expects "the last common ancestor of all placental mammals" or "the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria." Let's answer accordingly.
